correctness.rationale: For any fixed k distinct target s-sets, projecting H_t to its intersection with their finite union gives an exact finite reversible chain. Its limit is a pure-death chain with a unique eigenvalue one. The stationary entrance flux into the forbidden states is k binom(r-1,s-1)/binom(n,s)+O(n^(-s-1)), including overlapping targets. The bounded mean-zero inverse for I-P_n and killed-chain Perron eigenvalue give the same leading escape rate; a uniform spectral gap over finitely many overlap patterns yields survival m^(-k)e^(-kx)(1+o(1)). Factorial moments give Poisson/Gumbel, and a one-target summable tail establishes mean. Independent small Johnson-walk trajectories matched the projected safe-chain survival through five steps.
residual_risks: Finite checks alone cannot establish unrestricted theorem; proof mechanisms and stated boundaries reviewed.

final_claim: For stationary simple Johnson walk on r-subsets with fixed integers 1<=s<r, the unseen s-subset count at t=(binom(n,s)/binom(r-1,s-1))(log binom(n,s)+x) tends to Poisson(e^-x), and the shadow cover time has centered Gumbel law and first-order expectation binom(n,s)log binom(n,s)/binom(r-1,s-1).
